title: Shami Takes Four Wickets, Backs Bhuvneshwar, and Questions His Own Exclusion
excerpt: Bengal's 36-year-old seamer returned 4 for 30 against Delhi at Kalyani, then argued Bhuvneshwar Kumar's New Zealand recall should have come long ago.
body:
• Mohammed Shami took 4 for 30 in 17.3 overs, with nine maidens, as Bengal bowled Delhi out for 240 at Kalyani on October 11.
  • Shami said Bhuvneshwar Kumar, recalled at 36 for India's T20I tour of New Zealand, should have been picked much earlier after back-to-back IPL seasons.
  • Shami's own last India appearance was on March 9, 2025, and he pushed back when reporters questioned his fitness.
  • Bengal's pace group also included Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar, with Aamir Gani taking 3 for 45.

Mohammed Shami made his point with the ball first and with words second on Sunday, October 11. Bowling for Bengal in their Ranji Trophy opener against Delhi at the Bengal Cricket Academy Ground in Kalyani, the 36-year-old fast bowler returned 4 for 30 from 17.3 overs, including nine maidens, as Delhi were bowled out for 240 in their first innings.

After play, Shami backed fellow fast bowler Bhuvneshwar Kumar's recall for India's T20I tour of New Zealand, while making clear he thought the call had come late. He was quoted as saying: "Bhuvi should have been picked a long time ago." Shami pointed to Bhuvneshwar's back-to-back performances in the Indian Premier League as the basis for selection, arguing that hard work and potential should not be kept waiting.

What happened in Kalyani

Delhi never settled for long against a Bengal attack built around pace. Reports of the day's play described Shami spreading his work across short spells in hot, humid conditions and still keeping control of the scoring. Hrithik Shokeen, batting at number eight, top-scored for Delhi with 56, while Ayush Doseja made 45 and Sarthak Ranjan made 33.

The support around Shami mattered. Off-spinner Aamir Gani took 3 for 45, Akash Deep took 2 for 74 and Mukesh Kumar took 1 for 43. Shami finished the innings by removing Shokeen, caught by Sudip Chatterjee, after earlier dismissals that included Yash Dhull and Doseja. The figures, at an economy rate below two runs an over, stood out on a surface Shami described as slower than Bengal had expected.

He also raised the pitch, saying a pace attack that also included Akash Deep, Mukesh Kumar and Ishan Porel deserved a more helpful wicket.

Context: two veterans, different outcomes

Bhuvneshwar Kumar, also 36, is back in India's T20I squad for the New Zealand tour after a long absence from the national side. His last India appearance before the recall was in November 2022, also in New Zealand, according to coverage of Shami's comments. His return followed strong IPL seasons for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, including, in one account, finishing as the second-leading wicket-taker in IPL 2026 with 28 wickets.

Shami's recent history is different. He returned in early 2025 after a 14-month injury layoff and played his last match for India on March 9, 2025, an ODI against New Zealand. Since then he has continued in domestic cricket for Bengal without a recall, even as he says his performances and fitness should be judged by what happens on the field.

Asked about his fitness at Kalyani, Shami told reporters to look at his bowling and write what they saw, adding that he was on the ground and playing wherever he was given a chance. Reports also noted a sarcastic edge when he was asked about his own prospects, underlining frustration rather than a formal claim for selection.

Analysis: why the comment landed

Shami's defence of Bhuvneshwar works on two levels. On its face, it is a senior player welcoming back a longtime colleague whose game, like his own, relies on swing, accuracy and experience rather than public campaigning. Shami described Bhuvneshwar as a quiet worker, making the point that a player does not need to talk constantly to deserve recognition.

Underneath that, the timing is hard to miss. If a 36-year-old seam bowler can be recalled after four years on the strength of sustained IPL form, then the route back cannot be closed on age alone. Shami did not need to name himself to make that argument. His 17.3 overs, nine maidens and four wickets on the same weekend supplied the rest of the case.

The limits are clear. A Ranji Trophy day is not a T20 international, and selectors will weigh format and workload, not one domestic spell alone.

What is next

For Bengal, the immediate task is to convert Delhi's 240 into a first-innings lead and points from the Group C opener. For Shami, the pattern is now familiar: keep bowling long, economical spells in domestic cricket and let each performance reopen the question.

Bhuvneshwar's series in New Zealand will be watched closely for what it signals about veteran seam bowlers. If he succeeds, the precedent helps experienced performers including Shami.
